Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for seeing this 5-year-old boy, Liam, for a multidisciplinary assessment. He was brought to my clinic by his parents, who are seeking further evaluation for his complex cutaneous, visual, and developmental concerns.

Liam has broad delays across his motor, speech, and cognitive domains, though he remains engaged and attentive, showing no features of encephalopathy. In the office, he demonstrated prominent light aversion, shielding his eyes from ambient illumination. A recent slit-lamp evaluation revealed bilateral lenticular opacifications. 

His cutaneous examination is notable for diffuse, adherent fish-skin-like scaling across his trunk and extremities, accompanied by well-demarcated scaly erythematous plaques on his torso and limbs. I also appreciated prominent spiny follicular plugs on his thighs and forearms. Liam has extensive scalp hair thinning with noticeable patches of bare skin. His nail borders are chronically tender, swollen, and inflamed. Orally, there is distinct erythema and swelling along his gingival margins, with deep cracked fissures at both oral commissures; his buccal and palatal mucosae remain healthy, with no evidence of stomatitis.

His chest was clear to auscultation, heart sounds were normal, and the abdomen was soft and non-tender. Family history is non-contributory, and his older sister is well. Recent laboratory investigations showed an unremarkable metabolic panel and complete blood count, and his plasma zinc concentration was entirely normal. He is managed primarily with regular topical emollient creams. 

I would be very grateful for your expert input regarding this presentation and your guidance on further diagnostic investigations.

Warm regards,

Dr. Arthur Vance
Department of Pediatrics
